title: The Three Rules for إِنَّ and أَنَّ, the Days of the Week, and Drilling the مُضَارِع Chart
summary: Starting on page 89, students recall the three rules that decide between إِنَّ and أَنَّ — sentence-initial, after a verb, and the قَالَ exception — and apply them across tamrīn 9, with the teacher showing how the same rule settles the wording of the adhān and the shahādah. The session then reviews the seven days of the week and moves into lesson 13, whose chart is a reduced version of the مُضَارِع table the class already has, lacking only the dual.
key_points: Three rules govern the choice: إِنَّ opens a sentence, أَنَّ comes after a preceding word or verb, and the one exception is after قَالَ or يَقُول, where إِنَّ returns.

This is why the adhān and the shahādah are أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ — أَشْهَدُ is a verb, so أَنَّ follows. Saying إِنَّ there is incorrect, and knowing the rule lets you hear the mistake.
إِنَّ puts the noun following it into the accusative — إِنَّ مُحَمَّدًا, إِنَّ اللَّهَ.
أَظُنُّ (aẓunnu : I think) is one of the verbs that takes أَنَّ after it: أَظُنُّ أَنَّكَ مِنْ بَاكِسْتَان.
Adding سَـ to a مُضَارِع verb makes it the near future: يَرْجِعُ (he returns) becomes سَيَرْجِعُ (he will return).

جَمْع الْمُؤَنَّث السَّالِم — the sound feminine plural on the ـَات pattern such as سَيِّئَات، سَمَاوَات، بَنَات — takes a kasra where the accusative fatḥa would be expected, as in خَلَقَ اللَّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ. The teacher was candid that there is no deeper reason; it is simply how the Arabs spoke.
Numbers reverse gender against their counted noun: صَفْحَة (ṣafḥah : page) is feminine, so eighty-nine becomes تِسْعٌ وَثَمَانُونَ rather than تِسْعَةٌ وَثَمَانُونَ.
When counting with nothing specific in mind, the feminine series is the default — وَاحِد، اثْنَان، ثَلَاثَة، أَرْبَعَة، خَمْسَة.

The seven days: يَوْم الْأَحَد (Sunday), يَوْم الِاثْنَيْن (Monday), يَوْم الثُّلَاثَاء (Tuesday), يَوْم الْأَرْبِعَاء (Wednesday), يَوْم الْخَمِيس (Thursday), يَوْم الْجُمُعَة (Friday), يَوْم السَّبْت (Saturday) — worth memorising, not least because the aḥādīth on fasting Mondays and Thursdays use them.
Lesson 13's chart gives the مُضَارِع across third, second and first person in singular and plural, but omits the dual, which the class already has from the fuller chart.
Addressing one female uses تَفْعَلِينَ — تَذْهَبِينَ، تَقُولِينَ — while تَذْهَبُونَ addresses a group of males and يَذْهَبْنَ speaks about a group of females.
The vowel on a verb's middle letter in the مُضَارِع cannot be deduced; it has to be learned word by word.

Vocabulary: وَزِير الْخَارِجِيَّة (foreign minister), غَدًا (tomorrow) against الْيَوْم (today) and أَمْس (yesterday), مَلْعَب (playground or any place of play), سَيَّارَة الْأُجْرَة (taxi, literally the car of the fee), مَصْنَع (factory), حَافِلَة (bus), and سَيِّدِي (my master, as a term of respect).
questions: [00:01:00] Q: If you are just counting with nothing specific in mind, which gender of number do you use? — A: Either is permissible, but people normally use the feminine series — ثَلَاثَة، أَرْبَعَة، خَمْسَة — so treat that as the default.
[00:05:01] Q: What does إِنَّ do to the word after it? — A: It gives it a fatḥa, though not necessarily the immediately following word in every construction.
[00:06:00] Q: What does مَا do here? — A: It negates, so مَا جَاءَ means he did not come.

[00:11:05] Q: Why does the sound feminine plural take a kasra instead of a fatḥa — what is the reason? — A: There is no deeper reason; it is simply the way the Arabs used it, and it is why السَّمَاوَاتِ appears with a kasra despite being the object.
[00:13:04] Q: Isn't it أَنَّ, since it comes after a verb? — A: Normally yes, but قَالَ and يَقُول are the exception, and there إِنَّ is used.
[00:27:00] Q: What does سَيِّدِي mean? — A: My master or my leader, used as a statement of respect.
[00:30:06] Q: How do we know the vowel on the middle letter of the مُضَارِع? — A: It cannot be guessed; it is simply something you have to know for each verb.
[00:17:03] Q: What is missing from the lesson 13 chart? — A: The dual forms; everything else — third, second and first person, singular and plural — is there.

quiz.q: Which form is used at the very start of a sentence?
options: Neither; a verb must come first
quiz.a: The first of the three rules: sentence-initial position takes إِنَّ.

quiz.q: Which form follows a preceding verb such as سَمِعْتُ or أَظُنُّ?
quiz.a: After a verb the form becomes أَنَّ — سَمِعْتُ أَنَّ، أَظُنُّ أَنَّكَ.

quiz.q: What is the one exception to the rule about following a verb?
options: After قَالَ or يَقُول, where إِنَّ is used
quiz.a: The teacher singled out قَالَ / يَقُول and anything on that pattern as the exception that keeps إِنَّ.

quiz.q: Why is the shahādah أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ and not أَشْهَدُ إِنَّ?
options: Because مُحَمَّدًا is in the accusative
Because أَشْهَدُ is a verb, so أَنَّ must follow
Because it is the start of a sentence
Because أَشْهَدُ is on the pattern of قَالَ
quiz.a: The teacher used this to show the rule's practical value: أَشْهَدُ is a verb and is not قَالَ, so the correct form is أَنَّ.

quiz.q: How is eighty-nine expressed when counting صَفْحَة?
quiz.a: صَفْحَة is feminine, and numbers reverse gender with their counted noun, so the masculine-looking تِسْعٌ is used.

quiz.q: What does سَـ do when attached to يَرْجِعُ?
options: Makes it the near future — he will return
quiz.a: سَيَرْجِعُ means he will return, which is how the news sentence about the foreign minister was translated.

quiz.q: Why does السَّمَاوَاتِ carry a kasra in خَلَقَ اللَّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ even though it is the object?
options: Because it is جَمْع الْمُؤَنَّث السَّالِم, which substitutes kasra for the accusative fatḥa
Because it is a مُضَاف إِلَيْهِ
Because it is a proper noun
quiz.a: The sound feminine plural on the ـَات pattern takes a kasra in place of the fatḥa — the rule the teacher restated here.
From خَمْسَة (five): الْخَمِيس is Thursday, the day paired with Monday in the aḥādīth on fasting.

quiz.q: Addressing one female, which form of ذَهَبَ is correct?
quiz.a: فِي أَيِّ سَاعَةٍ تَذْهَبِينَ إِلَى الْجَامِعَةِ يَا عَائِشَة — second-person feminine singular takes ـِينَ.

quiz.q: What does سَيَّارَة الْأُجْرَة mean literally?
options: The car of the fee, that is, a taxi
quiz.a: أُجْرَة is a fee or wage, so سَيَّارَة الْأُجْرَة is the car you pay a fare for — a taxi.

quran_examples.translation: Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar.
quran_examples.note: Illustrates the first rule: at the opening of a sentence the form is إِنَّ, here with the attached pronoun as إِنَّا.

quran_examples.translation: And know that Allah is with those who fear Him.
quran_examples.note: Illustrates the second rule: following the verb اعْلَمُوا the form becomes أَنَّ, and اللَّهَ takes the fatḥa that أَنَّ requires.

quran_examples.arabic: قَالَ إِنِّي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ آتَانِيَ الْكِتَابَ وَجَعَلَنِي نَبِيًّا
quran_examples.transliteration: qāla innī ʿabdu llāhi ātāniya al-kitāba wa-jaʿalanī nabiyyā
quran_examples.translation: He said: Indeed, I am a servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet.
quran_examples.note: Illustrates the exception: after قَالَ the form reverts to إِنَّ, here as إِنِّي — spoken by ʿĪsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام.

quran_examples.arabic: اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً
quran_examples.transliteration: allāhu alladhī khalaqa al-samāwāti wa-l-arḍa wa-anzala mina al-samāʾi māʾā
quran_examples.translation: It is Allah who created the heavens and the earth and sent down rain from the sky.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's own example for جَمْع الْمُؤَنَّث السَّالِم: السَّمَاوَاتِ is the object yet takes a kasra, while الْأَرْضَ beside it takes the ordinary fatḥa.

quran_examples.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
quran_examples.transliteration: inna llāha ʿalā kulli shayʾin qadīr
quran_examples.translation: Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
quran_examples.note: Shows what the class observed about إِنَّ putting the following noun in the accusative: اللَّهَ carries a fatḥa after it.
